what: Lid camera still after @mcwilliams03 reported the focus thumbscrew at the end of its travel with the picture still blurred, 2026-10-22
still: still_2147Z_plate_fills_frame.jpg (saved at half resolution); figure blur_triangle_2147Z.jpg
how: curl -s localhost:8081/still and /status on the lid camera Pi while the stream ran (picam_source.py); stream untouched
ot2: rail lights on (GET /robot/lights), no protocol run and no maintenance run
focus_score_note: at analogue gain 15.8 the score is mostly sensor noise, so it can't guide focusing in this state

zoom.plate_footprint_px: about 3600 x 2450 (127.76 x 85.48 mm), so about 28-29 px/mm
zoom.estimate_mm: about 27 (26.6 px/mm at 25 mm); the plate-in-box target is 27.7 mm

blur.well: a yellow well, 6.86 mm = 196 px, spreads to a rounded triangle about 330 px across; the triangle is the iris's shape
blur.blur_spot_estimate: roughly 150-250 px, 0.2-0.4 mm on the 1.55 um pixels
blur.per_channel: green 1-4 % narrower than red and blue on all four plate edges; too small and too lens-dependent to say which side of focus the sensor is on

iris: Lux 5.9 at exposure 66.7 ms and gain 15.8 (both at the auto-exposure limits), against 87.9 at 47.8 ms and gain 2.0 for the sharp still of 2026-10-20 03:58 UTC, also with the rail lights on. Allowing 2-3x for a dark plate filling the frame instead of the light deck, the iris is about 2-3 stops more closed than on 20 Oct
defocus_estimate_mm: blur spot x f-number: 0.2-0.4 mm x about f/5.6-11 = roughly 1-4 mm between where the image forms and the sensor

focus_ring_model.basis: thin lens; plate about 0.6 m from the lens; Waveshare's minimum object distance 0.20 m; image shift from infinity = f^2/(u - f)

at_27_mm.plate_on_the_ring: about a third of the way from FAR to NEAR

reading: With the lens seated at the standard C-mount spacing, the plate is in the focus ring's range at every zoom, about a third of the way from FAR at 27 mm. A blur spot this size at the end of the ring, and at 21:10 a 1.3 mm blur circle at a wide zoom, where no focus setting can be more than 0.2-0.5 mm off (that needs 1.8 mm or more even at f/1.4), say the lens-to-sensor spacing has changed since the sharp stills of 20 Oct: the lens or the C-CS adapter backed out of its thread (0.79 mm a turn), the camera's back-focus ring screwed out, or a second (or no) C-CS adapter. Which end the focus thumbscrew stopped at gives the direction: FAR = lens too far from the sensor, NEAR = too close.
